title: Content Delivery Networks
overview: A Content Delivery Network (CDN) is a geographically distributed network of servers (Points of Presence / PoPs) that cache content closer to end users. Instead of every request traveling to the origin server, users are served from the nearest edge node — dramatically reducing latency for static assets, and increasingly for dynamic content and APIs.
keyPoints: Reduces latency by serving content from servers geographically close to users
Offloads bandwidth from origin servers — can absorb 90%+ of traffic
Provides DDoS protection and WAF capabilities at the edge
SSL/TLS termination at the edge reduces handshake overhead
Cache-Control headers control what CDNs cache and for how long
Edge computing (Cloudflare Workers, Lambda@Edge) enables running logic at PoPs

concepts.name: Origin Pull
concepts.description: CDN fetches content from origin on first request, then caches it at the edge. Cache-Control headers determine TTL. Most common CDN model.

concepts.name: Origin Push
concepts.description: Content is proactively pushed to CDN edge nodes before users request it. Ensures instant availability but requires managing CDN as a deployment target.

concepts.name: Cache Invalidation
concepts.description: When origin content changes, CDN cache must be invalidated. Options: wait for TTL expiry, send purge API calls, or use cache-busting URLs (versioned filenames).

concepts.name: Anycast Routing
concepts.description: CDN uses Anycast to route users to the nearest PoP at the network layer. The same IP address is announced from multiple locations; routing protocols find the nearest one.

tools.name: Cloudflare
tools.description: Most widely used CDN/WAF, global network, free tier, powerful edge computing with Workers

tools.name: AWS CloudFront
tools.description: AWS-integrated CDN with Lambda@Edge, origins can be S3, ALB, or custom servers

tools.name: Fastly
tools.description: Instant purging, real-time analytics, popular with media companies and SaaS

tools.name: Akamai
tools.description: Largest CDN by PoP count, enterprise-focused with advanced security features

tradeoffs: CDNs are nearly always beneficial for static assets. The trade-off is cache freshness — longer TTLs reduce origin load but serve stale content longer. Use versioned file names (e.g., app.abc123.js) for cache-busting without manual purges. Dynamic content caching (API responses) requires careful consideration of cache keys to avoid serving one user's data to another.
interviewTips: Mention CDNs early in any system design involving global users — it's a quick win for latency
Discuss cache-busting strategies for deployments: versioned URLs vs. ETags vs. manual purges
CDNs also provide DDoS mitigation — mention this for high-traffic or public-facing systems
Edge computing at CDN PoPs can reduce origin load further for personalized content
